notes.title: Update 1.6
notes.notes:
Hello, Game Builders!

We’re excited to bring you Update 1.6, packed with highly requested features and improvements. Let’s dive into what’s new:

🔹 No More Forced Retirement!
You can now play as long as you want without worrying about forced retirement. Keep building, expanding, and refining your games without unnecessary interruptions!

🔹 Trending Themes Feature
Introducing trending themes—now you can explore and create games based on trends, adding more variety and strategic depth. Games built on trending themes will also receive a sales bonus!

🔹 Q1 Roadmap Completed!
We’ve successfully delivered all planned features from Q1 of our roadmap, and we’re now preparing for the exciting next phase. Thank you for your support and feedback!

Stay tuned for more updates, and as always, happy game building! 🚀

notes.title: Game builder tycoon Future
notes.notes:
Hello, Game Builders!

We’re excited to share our 2025 Roadmap for Game Builder Tycoon! This year, we’re introducing new features, enhancements, and deeper gameplay mechanics to make your game development experience even better.

Here’s what’s coming:

Q1 (Before April)
Sandbox Mode – Keep playing even after retirement! No more forced endings.
Trending Themes & Genres – Stay updated with dynamically changing trends to strategize your game releases.

Q2 (Before July)
Room Customization – Personalize your game studio with your choice of floor and walls.
Furniture Placement – Arrange your office for a better workflow.
Visual Changes – Better lighting and an overall improved look.
Select Predefined Engines – Choose from prebuilt game engines for more strategic decision-making while creating your games.
Game Optimization – Improved performance so your computers can run this game smoothly with reduced fan noise, reduce lags and overheating issues.

Q3 (Before October)
Create Custom Engines – Design and develop your own game engines!
Create Consoles – Design and launch your own gaming consoles.

Q4 (End of December)
Better Sounds & Music – Improved audio system for an immersive experience.
Publisher Mode – Take on the role of a game publisher and manage studios under your wing.

This roadmap lays the foundation for an exciting year, but we’re always listening to your feedback! If you have ideas or suggestions, feel free to share them in the comments or on our Discord server.

notes.title: Update 1.5: Weather Update
notes.notes:
We are excited to announce the release of version 1.5, a quick yet significant update that enhances your gameplay experience with dynamic weather visuals! From January to December, you'll experience a range of weather changes, including snowy winters, sunny summers, refreshing rains, vibrant spring, and golden autumn.

Each weather type comes with tailored sound effects and VFX, adding more depth and realism to your adventures.

Devlog
We’re committed to making the game even better, and future updates are on the way. However, please note that upcoming updates may take some time as we work on adding more exciting content. Stay tuned, and thank you for your continued support!

notes.title: Major Update 1.4 ( new features)
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! We're thrilled to announce the release of Major Update 1.4 for Game Builder Tycoon! This update brings exciting new features and improvements to enhance your game development experience:

[h1]Theme Expansion:[/h1] We've added 21 new themes and replaced 2 old ones, giving you a total of 42 themes (19 old, 23 new) to choose from for your games.

[h1]Price System Overhaul:[/h1] Introducing a more detailed pricing system! Now you can set the price of your game based on recommendations influenced by your company’s reputation, game size, and selected features. Use a slider to adjust the price and watch how it affects sales dynamics—raising the price decreases sales and lowering it increases them.

[h1]Mood System:[/h1] Choose from 6 different moods, ranging from relaxing to horror, to match the vibe of your game. This new feature allows for more creative customization and depth.

[h1]Detailed Report Generation:[/h1] Once a game is complete, generate a detailed report to understand areas where your game could improve. You can also research game reports or view past reports in your game history.

[h1]Difficulty Balancing:[/h1] We've made the game slightly more challenging in terms of review scores, offering a more engaging and rewarding gameplay experience.

Note: Detailed reports will only work for new games created in this latest build. Older games from your game history (created before this update) will not generate reports correctly. We recommend starting a new game to experience this feature fully.

for example: you created game X in version 1.3 and want to unlock the report so it will not generate a report of game X correctly.

notes.title: Update 1.3
notes.notes:
We are excited to announce the release of version 1.3, bringing new features and improvements to your gameplay experience!

Difficulty Options: You can now choose your difficulty level when starting a new game! Select from Easy to Hard, with difficulty levels affecting both your game rating and your earnings.

Extra Points: Players now receive 2 additional points when creating their character at the start of the game, allowing for more customization and flexibility in your journey.

Full Refund: Cancelling a game development now returns 100% of your invested money! Previously, only 50% was refunded, but now you can recover all of your funds if you decide to change your project.

Thank you for your continued support, and we hope these updates improve your gameplay experience. As always, happy developing!

notes.title: New Features added and devlog 2
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! We’ve updated the game to Version 1.2. Here’s a quick look at what’s new:

[h1]Character Info Added:[/h1]
When you update your character, you will now have a clear idea of how good or bad your character compares to industry standards. Just open the character update screen, and the info will be right there.

[h1]Hint for Sliders:[/h1]
A new hint option has been added for sliders that can be toggled on or off. This will show two random fields, such as what your game might need in a specific slider. Check this out in the slider section — don’t miss out!

[h1]Easy Free-to-Play Sales:[/h1]
We’ve slightly improved free-to-play sales mechanics.

[h1]Genre-Theme Description:[/h1]
Now when you hover over a genre or theme, a helpful description will pop up.

[h1]Devlog 2:[/h1]
Hey everyone, sorry that I couldn’t add too many new features in this update due to health issues. However, we have lots of exciting plans for the next update, including:

A Difficulty Option, since some players find the game too easy while others find it hard.
A Detailed Research Report to help you better understand feedback.
After this, we might start planning something big... Maybe you’ll even be able to create your own console!

notes.title: Upcoming Features and Devlog #1
notes.notes:
We are excited to share with you some of the new features that will be introduced in our next update:

[h1]Upcoming Features:[/h1]

[h3]In-Game Detailed Reports:[/h3] A comprehensive new feature that provides players with a detailed breakdown of what went wrong in their previous game and suggestions for improvement in their next attempt. This will help you refine your strategy and optimize your decisions.

[h3]Industry Skill Bar:[/h3] A visual representation of how your character's current skill set stacks up against industry standards. You'll be able to see whether your character is competitive or if they need additional training to keep up with evolving demands.

[h3]Genre and Theme Descriptions:[/h3] We'll be adding in-depth descriptions for genres and themes to help you better understand what each one entails, ensuring that your creative choices align with your vision and strategy.

[h1]Devlog:[/h1]

It has been a year since I started this project, driven by my passion for game development and the desire to showcase the journey of creating a game. My goal has always been to strike a balance between accessibility and depth, making this game enjoyable for both newcomers and veterans of the management/simulation genre.

As a solo developer (although I have a team, the development work is done by me alone), the project has undergone numerous changes, primarily based on the invaluable feedback received from our players. Even though this game hasn't launched in Early Access, I am committed to continually refining and improving it.

I’m aware that some of the current localization may not be perfect in all languages, and I assure you that we are working hard to improve this over time. Your patience and support mean the world to me, and I’m confident we’ll continue making this game even better in the future.

Thank you for being a part of this journey!

notes.title: Game Rating & Sales FAQ answered
notes.notes:
[h3]Why My Game Gets a Bad Rating, How to Find What's wrong [FAQ][/h3]
There may be multiple reasons, but here’s a guide to help you understand why your game might receive a bad rating.

[h1]FIRST CHECK [/h1]
First, consider the combination of genre, theme, art style, and viewpoint. While it's okay for these elements to be unconventional, make sure they're not completely mismatched. If your combination is totally off, then it might moderately affect your rating. So, it’s okay if things aren’t perfect—just avoid having completely mismatched combinations. Think of real-world examples where games with unique combinations still make sense.

[h1]SECOND CHECK[/h1]
Next, examine the slider and subcategory values (e.g., optimization, UI, visuals). Ensure that none of these values are too unusual or poorly balanced. it's okay to be not perfect. Just like in real-world game development, things should be aligned reasonably. If everything checks out here, move on to the final and most crucial aspect: character skills.

[h1]LAST MOST IMPORTANT CHECK[/h1]
If your characters' skills are outdated or not in line with industry standards, this could be a significant reason for the bad rating. We recommend regularly training your characters based on your budget. A good rule of thumb is that characters should improve by about 5% each year. Evaluate the timing and frequency of training to keep your characters competitive.

[h2]Understanding the Importance of Character Skills[/h2]
In Game Builder Tycoon, one key to success is keeping your characters' skills in line with the game's evolving challenges. Poorly skilled characters can severely impact the final quality of your games, directly influencing ratings.

Every year, your characters should be improving by at least 5%, whether it's in technical expertise, creative skills, or overall productivity. To make the most of your training budget, plan the timing of upgrades carefully. For instance, training just before starting a major project or improving specific skills that align with your current game’s requirements can significantly boost the overall rating.

Moreover, investing in the right character skills at the right time ensures that your games not only meet but exceed the industry’s expectations, helping you achieve higher ratings and, ultimately, better sales.


[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
It's okay if your genre, theme, viewpoint, art style, sliders, and subcategories aren't perfect. Don't stress over trying to get everything aligned flawlessly. Just be mindful of these aspects and ensure they make sense in the context of your game. Remember, half of your game's rating heavily depends on your character skills. Keeping your characters trained and up to industry standards will go a long way in boosting your ratings. Focus on gradual improvements, and you’ll see the results over time.

You can check the same for sales in the discussion tab, thank you.

notes.title: AI ART REMOVED
notes.notes:
Previously, we used a mix of AI-generated art and manually created art for various visual elements such as Steam imagery and in-game assets. However, we have now replaced all AI-generated images with 3D renderings created entirely by our team. These new images are used across the Steam store, main menu, loading screens, and any other visual aspects of the game.

In short, no AI images remain in the game—all visuals are original creations made by our talented team!
